memes initiated by high-status members do not spread faster, and memes that are consistent with the theme spread faster, in the context of virtual communities

memes initiated by high-status members are not always more successful than memes initiated by lowstatus members, but memes that are consistent with the forum theme are more successful than inconsistent memes.

the influence of meme content on the spread of information in social networks.
the role of social status in the diffusion of memes and the role of meme content in the spread of ideas in virtual communities.
the spread of information in online communities and the role of status and consistency in the spread of ideas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the status of meme initiators does not influence meme spread, but that meme spread is influenced by the status of the initiator.
memes that are consistent with a forum’s theme and initiated by a low-status member spread faster than memes inconsistent with a theme and initiated by high- or moderate-status members.
memes started by low-status members and memes consistent with a forum's theme are spread more frequently than other memes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
low-status members are more successful at initiating memes in online communities than high- and moderate-status members.
the status of the initiator of a meme does not affect the spread of the meme in a group.

memes initiated by high-status members were not necessarily more likely to be adopted by others, and that low-status members were not more likely to adopt memes that are inconsistent with the theme of a forum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
low-status group member memes spread more rapidly than high-status member memes.
the status of the meme initiator is more important than the consistency of the meme content in determining its spread in virtual communities.
the status of the member who initiates a meme is not a strong predictor of the meme’s popularity.
